memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty; walk before me faithfully and be blameless." - Gen 17:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Thirteen silent years have passed since Ishmael's birth. Abram is now ninety-nine, and Sarai still has no child of promise. Any human hope of descendants has long since faded. And into that impossibility, God appears with a new name for Himself: "I am God Almighty" - El Shaddai, the All-Sufficient One, the God of more-than-enough.

The timing is everything. God waits until Abram is well past any natural ability to father a child, and then reveals Himself as Almighty. God often lets us come to the end of our own strength before He shows us the fullness of His. When we can do nothing, we are finally ready to see that He can do everything.

Notice what God asks in response: "walk before me faithfully and be blameless." This isn't a demand to earn the promise - the covenant that follows is pure gift. It is a call to live in the light of who God is. Because He is Almighty, Abram can walk in wholehearted trust.

That is the order of the gospel too: God reveals His all-sufficiency, and out of that we live faithfully - not to earn His favour, but in response to it. Whatever impossibility you face, the God who meets you there is El Shaddai. "Is anything too hard for the Lord?" (Gen 18:14). Where you have run out, He is more than enough.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you come to the end of your own strength?
- What would change if you truly believed God is "more than enough"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
God Almighty, when I have run out of my own strength, remind me that You are more than enough. Help me walk before You in wholehearted trust, resting in Your all-sufficiency.
Amen.
